property_summary: For any caller and any supplied _unlockTime and msg.value, after a successful Put the stored unlockTime is never less than the current block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it in the past, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

After any call to Put by any address with any paid value and any _unlockTime, the contract's stored unlockTime for that address is never strictly less than the block.timestamp at the time Put returned; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it in the past and thus violate acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime.

For any caller and any paid value, after Put returns the stored unlockTime is either unchanged from before or at least block.timestamp (i.e., Put never decreases unlockTime below current time); the mutant that blindly assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can decrease an existing future unlockTime to a past value, violating this monotonic/non-decreasing-with-respect-to-now property for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller, after Put returns the stored unlockTime for that caller is always >= the current block.timestamp; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it below block.timestamp, violating this invariant for some fuzzed _unlockTime.

For any caller, calling Put with any _unlockTime and any payable value never makes the stored unlockTime for that caller be strictly less than the previous stored unlockTime when the previous stored unlockTime was already >= block.timestamp; the mutant can decrease an existing non-past unlockTime to an earlier (past) value, violating monotonicity when prior unlockTime >= now.

For any depositor and deposit amount, calling Put(_unlockTime) sets the account's unlockTime to at least the provided _unlockTime (i.e., max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp can violate this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any depositor and any _unlockTime, after Put the stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp and >= the pre-call block.timestamp and if the caller provided an _unlockTime in the future (> pre-call timestamp) then the stored unlockTime will be >= that provided value; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate that when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any depositor and any candidate unlock timestamp, after calling Put the contract's stored unlockTime for that depositor equals the maximum of the provided _unlockTime and the block.timestamp at call time; the mutant that forces unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate this when the caller supplies a future _unlockTime.

For any depositor and any provided _unlockTime, if the depositor calls Put with a future _unlockTime (greater than the current block.timestamp) and sends a positive value, then after Put the stored unlockTime for that depositor equals the provided _unlockTime; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp will violate this for some such inputs.

For any depositor sending a positive ether value and providing a future _unlockTime (> block.timestamp), the reference sets Acc[msg].unlockTime to that provided future timestamp, whereas the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp will sometimes set a strictly smaller value, breaking this property.

After any account calls Put with some msg.value, the contract's Acc[caller].balance is at least msg.value more than its previous value (i.e., Put preserves and increments previous balance by msg.value); the mutant that sets balance = msg.value breaks this when caller already had a non-zero balance.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling Put the holder's recorded balance is at least the deposited msg.value (i.e., acc.balance >= msg.value); the mutant that overwrites instead of increments can make acc.balance < msg.value when the prior balance was larger and msg.value is smaller, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount (including zero), after calling Put the recorded balance for that depositor is at least the deposit amount plus the previous balance (i.e., Put increments the stored balance by msg.value); the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value (overwriting previous balance) can make this fail when the depositor already had a positive previous balance and then sends a smaller deposit.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, calling Put increases the depositor's stored balance by exactly the deposited msg.value (i.e., Acc[depositor].balance_after == Acc[depositor].balance_before + msg.value); the mutant that assigns acc.balance = msg.value instead of adding breaks this when the depositor already has a positive balance and then deposits a smaller amount.

For any actor and deposit amount, if the actor's prior recorded balance is zero then after calling Put with that deposit the recorded balance equals the deposit (acc.balance == msg.value); the mutant that overwrites rather than adds still satisfies this when prior balance is zero but the reference also satisfies it for all inputs — to distinguish, we instead require: if prior balance is non-zero and the deposit is zero, the reference preserves the prior non-zero balance (i.e., acc.balance_after == acc.balance_before) while the mutant may set it to zero (when msg.value == 0 it would overwrite with 0).

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put with that msg.value always increases the caller's recorded balance by exactly msg.value (and succeeds); the mutant adds require(msg.value >= MinSum) so small deposits revert and thus break this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, a successful call to Put always increases that caller's recorded Acc balance by exactly msg.value; the mutant requires msg.value >= MinSum causing small deposits to revert and thus breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value less than MinSum, the reference contract accepts the deposit (Put returns/succeeds) and increases Acc[caller].balance by msg.value, whereas the mutant rejects such small deposits (reverts), so there exist fuzzed small amounts that make the mutant fail while the reference succeeds.

For any caller and any deposit amount, a call to Put that completes (does not revert) leaves Acc[caller].balance equal to its prior value plus msg.value; the mutant causes some small msg.value calls that would succeed on the reference to revert, so there exist inputs where the mutant's Put call does not complete while the reference's does.

For any caller and any deposit amount, if calling Put with value v succeeds, then Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly v; the mutant rejects (reverts) some small v (< MinSum) that the reference accepts, so there exist inputs where the mutant's Put call fails while the reference's succeeds.

For every call Put(_unlockTime) funded with a nonzero msg.value by any sender, the reference contract always records that call in Log by increasing Log.History.length (i.e., Log receives an AddMessage), whereas the mutant that deleted the LogFile.AddMessage call will not increase Log.History.length for at least some inputs (any call with msg.value>0).

For every call to Put with msg.value > 0, the reference C always causes Log.History.length to increase by 1 (it records the deposit), whereas the mutant that deletes the LogFile.AddMessage call will not increase Log.History.length for such calls, so there exist inputs (any with msg.value>0) where the mutant violates this rule.

For every call to Put(...) (including via fallback) the reference C always makes a call to Log.AddMessage, so Log.History.length increases when Put is invoked with msg.value > 0, while the mutant that removed the AddMessage call will not increase History.length for such inputs.

For every call to Put by any sender sending a positive amount, the reference contract records the deposit by adding a Log.History entry (History.length increases), while the mutant that deletes the LogFile.AddMessage call will fail to increase History.length for at least some such inputs.

For every call to Put by any address with a positive msg.value, the reference contract appends a Log.Message (increasing Log.History.length) while the mutant that removed the LogFile.AddMessage call will not increase Log.History.length for such calls (so there exist inputs with msg.value>0 where the mutant violates this).

For every caller and amount, if their account balance in C is at least MinSum and at least the requested withdrawal amount, then calling Collect strictly after the stored unlockTime (block.timestamp > unlockTime) always allows the reference to transfer funds (succeeds), whereas the mutant allowing Collect when block.timestamp == unlockTime can change the observable outcome at that exact timestamp (the mutant can succeed at timestamp == unlockTime while the reference would not).

For any account and amounts, Collect should NOT succeed at block.timestamp == unlockTime (reference requires block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant that uses >= can allow a Collect to succeed exactly when block.timestamp equals unlockTime, violating this rule.

For any caller, amount and unlockTime setup where the caller's balance ≥ MinSum and ≥ requested amount, calling Collect at exactly block.timestamp == stored unlockTime must fail (reference requires block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant using >= can make that call succeed, so the property is that Collect invoked at timestamp == unlockTime does not transfer funds (call reverts or does not send) on the reference but may on the mutant.

For any actor, amount and stored unlockTime, calling Collect exactly at block.timestamp == unlockTime must NOT succeed in sending the requested funds on the reference (which requires block.timestamp > unlockTime), whereas the mutant that uses '>=' may allow the transfer to succeed at that exact timestamp.

For any actor/amount/unlockTime where the actor deposited ≥ MinSum and ≥ amount, calling Collect strictly after unlockTime (block.timestamp > unlockTime) always succeeds on the reference; the mutant that changes the check to >= can additionally allow Collect to succeed exactly at block.timestamp == unlockTime, so the reference preserves that Collect at timestamp == unlockTime does not succeed while the mutant may succeed.

For any caller and any amount _am, the reference contract never allows a Collect that reduces the caller's balance below MinSum (i.e., after a successful Collect either the caller's balance is unchanged or >= MinSum); the mutant removing the MinSum guard permits a Collect that leaves balance < MinSum for some inputs.

After any call to Collect by any account, the reference contract never leaves that account's stored balance strictly below MinSum (i.e. either Collect does not reduce the balance or leaves it >= MinSum); the mutant removing the MinSum check allows a Collect that results in stored balance < MinSum for some inputs.

For any caller, after calling Collect(_am) the reference contract ensures the caller's stored balance is never left below MinSum (Collect either doesn't run or leaves balance >= MinSum); the mutant removing the MinSum check allows a Collect that results in stored balance < MinSum for some inputs.

If a caller successfully Collects amount _am (call returns/succeeds) then in the reference contract either the call did nothing or the caller's on-chain ether balance (address(c).balance change is consistent) and the contract's stored Acc[msg.sender].balance after the call is >= 0 and, specifically, the reference never allows a successful Collect that transfers funds when the caller's stored balance before transfer was < MinSum (i.e., Collect will only succeed and transfer value when acc.balance >= MinSum), whereas the mutant can succeed transferring value even when acc.balance < MinSum causing a transfer that should be disallowed.

For any caller and any inputs, the reference contract never allows a Collect call to succeed (i.e., return normally) and transfer funds when the caller's stored balance before the call was strictly less than MinSum; the mutant removing the MinSum check permits a successful Collect that transfers funds even when the stored balance before the call < MinSum.

Invariant: After a successful Collect call by an honest holder, the contract's stored balance for that holder is decreased by the collected amount immediately (i.e., acc.balance == priorBalance - _am); the mutant that performs the external call before subtracting allows reentrancy to drain funds so this invariant can be violated for some inputs.

For any caller and amount admissible to Collect, after Collect returns the contract's recorded balance for that caller equals priorBalance - amount; the mutant that does the external call before subtracting enables a reentrant attacker to drain extra funds so this equality can be violated for some inputs.

After any Collect call that succeeds, the contract's recorded balance for the caller is decreased by exactly the collected amount (acc.balance_final == acc.balance_prior - _am); the mutant that moves the external call before updating balance allows reentrant draining so this equality can be violated for some inputs.

After any Collect call returns, the caller's recorded balance in C has decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount (i.e. acc.balance_final == acc.balance_prior - _am); a mutant that does the external call before subtracting allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw extra funds, violating this property for some inputs.

For any caller and amount where Collect is allowed, if the recipient re-enters during the external send, the correct contract always ends with recorded balance equal to prior minus the withdrawn amount (no extra loss), while the mutant that does the external call before updating balance allows reentrancy to drain extra funds and thus can make the final recorded balance less than prior-minus-withdrawn for some inputs.

For any depositor who deposited >= MinSum, a Collect(amount) call that meets the checks always transfers the ETH out and returns (no revert) when the recipient's fallback/receive succeeds; the mutant using send can fail (return false) when the recipient's fallback uses more than 2300 gas, causing a revert — so the reference never reverts while the mutant can for some recipient behaviors.

For any depositor/address and amount satisfying admissible preconditions, calling Collect succeeds (does not revert) on the reference contract C because external transfer via call forwards all gas; the mutant using send can cause the transfer to fail (send returns false) when the recipient's fallback consumes >2300 gas, causing Collect to revert — so the reference always returns ok=true while the mutant can produce ok=false for some adversarial recipient behavior.

For any caller who previously deposited at least MinSum and meets Collect preconditions, calling Collect(...) always completes (does not revert) on the reference contract; changing the external transfer to send can make the transfer fail for a malicious recipient whose fallback consumes >2300 gas, causing Collect to revert, so the mutant can cause Collect to revert while the reference never does.

For any depositor who has balance >= MinSum and requests Collect(_am) satisfying preconditions, the reference contract's Collect call always succeeds (does not revert) because it uses call to forward all gas; the mutant that uses send can fail (return false) when the recipient's fallback consumes >2300 gas causing Collect to revert, so there exist inputs (a depositor, amount, and a malicious receiver with expensive fallback) where the mutant reverts but the reference does not.

For any depositor and amount that satisfy Collect's guards, the reference C's Collect call always returns (does not revert) when sending ETH out (because it uses call forwarding all gas); the mutant that uses send can revert if the recipient's fallback/receive consumes >2300 gas, so there exists an adversarial recipient and fuzzed amount that makes the mutant revert while the reference does not.

For any caller and amount meeting the withdrawal preconditions, a successful low-level send in Collect either forwards the ETH and logs the Collect (leaving c.address balance decreased); the mutant can fail the external send but still deduct the caller's balance (state changed without funds transferred), so there exists inputs where c's stored balance decreased while contract ETH balance did not — the reference never loses ETH without a successful send.
